content: The effects of rifampin on various drugs are primarily mediated through its impact on hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly involving cytochrome P450 enzymes such as CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP1A2, and others, as well as drug transporters like P-glycoprotein (P-gp). Below is a detailed explanation of the interactions: 1. Rifampin and Ripretinib: Use alternative drugs or monitor closely. 2. Rifampin and Risperidone: Rifampin reduces risperidone levels via P-gp efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 3. Rifampin and Ritlecitinib: Rifampin decreases ritlecitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing efficacy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Rifampin and Ritonavir: Rifampin reduces ritonavir levels through P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Rifampin and Rivaroxaban: Rifampin decreases rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with strong P-gp and CYP3A4 inducers. If co-administration is necessary, consider increasing the rivaroxaban dose. 6. Rifampin and Roflumilast: Rifampin reduces roflumilast levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 metabolism, potentially reducing therapeutic effectiveness. Co-administration is contraindicated. 7. Rifampin and Rolapitant: Rifampin decreases rolapitant efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Rifampin and Romidepsin: Rifampin reduces romidepsin levels via P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Rifampin and Ropinirole: Rifampin decreases ropinirole levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Rifampin and Rosuvastatin: Rifampin increases rosuvastatin toxicity through OATP1B1 inhibition, raising the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 11. Rifampin and Ruxolitinib: Rifampin reduces ruxolitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Rifampin and Sacubitril/Valsartan: Rifampin increases valsartan levels via OATP1B1 inhibition. Monitor for adverse reactions and adjust therapy as needed. 13. Rifampin and Saxagliptin: Rifampin decreases saxagliptin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Rifampin and Seladelpar: Rifampin reduces seladelpar levels by increasing metabolism. Monitor biochemical response (e.g., ALP and bilirubin) during treatment. 15. Rifampin and Selegiline: Rifampin decreases selegiline levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Rifampin and Selexipag: Increase the selexipag dose up to twice the typical dose if co-administered. 17. Rifampin and Selpercatinib: Rifampin decreases selpercatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Rifampin and Sildenafil: Rifampin reduces sildenafil plasma levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, as efficacy may be significantly reduced. 19. Rifampin and Silodosin: Rifampin decreases silodosin levels via P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Rifampin and Simvastatin: Rifampin reduces simvastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism but may increase toxicity through OATP1B1 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Rifampin and Siponimod: Rifampin reduces siponimod levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. 22. Rifampin and Sirolimus: Rifampin decreases sirolimus levels via P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Rifampin and Sodium Bicarbonate: Rifampin absorption may be reduced by concomitant antacid use. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 24. Rifampin and Sofosbuvir: Rifampin reduces sofosbuvir levels by inducing P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing antiviral efficacy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Rifampin and Tadalafil: Rifampin reduces tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid in pulmonary hypertension patients and monitor erectile dysfunction patients for reduced response. 26. Rifampin and Tamoxifen: Rifampin reduces tamoxifen levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Rifampin and Tamsulosin: Rifampin decreases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 28. Rifampin and Tramadol: Rifampin reduces tramadol and its active metabolite levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Rifampin and Triazolam: Rifampin reduces triazolam levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Rifampin and Valsartan: Rifampin increases valsartan levels via OATP1B1 inhibition. Monitor for adverse reactions. 31. Rifampin and Vandetanib: Rifampin reduces vandetanib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 32. Rifampin and Vardenafil: Rifampin reduces vardenafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Rifampin and Velpatasvir: Rifampin reduces velpatasvir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Rifampin and Tizanidine: Rifampin reduces tizanidine levels via CYP1A2 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 35. Rifampin and Tocilizumab: Rifampin reduces tocilizumab levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 36. Rifampin and Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Rifampin reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 37. Rifampin and Upadacitinib: Rifampin reduces upadacitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 38. Rifampin and Valbenazine: Rifampin reduces valbenazine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Rifampin and Vemurafenib: Rifampin reduces vemurafenib levels via P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 40. Rifampin and Tofacitinib: Rifampin reduces tofacitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to reduced efficacy. Use caution and monitor. These interactions highlight the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when rifampin is co-administered with other medications.
